topStories.headline: Grocery Outlet Opens on Bay Street, Ending Three-Year Food Desert
topStories.dek: The new discount grocer fills the 30,000-square-foot void left by Safeway's 2023 closure, restoring full-service grocery access to some 20,000 nearby residents.
topStories.body:
North Beach and Fisherman's Wharf residents finally have a full-service grocery store again. Grocery Outlet opened August 14 at 350 Bay St. in the NorthPoint Shopping Center, ending a three-year gap created when Safeway shuttered the same location in 2023, saying the store did not meet financial expectations. Mayor Daniel Lurie attended a ribbon-cutting ceremony on opening day. "For many families, food has been difficult without a full-scale grocery store these past three years since the Safeway closed in 2023," Lurie said, according to SFist.

The new 30,000-square-foot store is independently owned and operated by Jacqueline and Joel Lanoie, who signed a 15-year lease on the space in early 2025, according to the SF Standard. The Lanoies, who grew up in California's Central Valley and now live in the Outer Sunset, had spent years working in the grocery industry before taking on the North Beach location. Grocery Outlet, the chain coincidentally celebrating its 80th anniversary around the same time it opened, was itself founded in San Francisco.

The store offers fresh produce, meat, dairy, household essentials, and discounted name-brand products — including, according to early shoppers, 80-cent avocados and $1.99 pita chips. The closure of the Safeway had left roughly 20,000 people within a half-mile of the site relying on a Trader Joe's across the street or making longer trips to stores along the Embarcadero or Market Street. The new Grocery Outlet joins Trader Joe's as the second major grocery anchor in the immediate area.

The opening comes amid a continuing wave of grocery closures elsewhere in San Francisco, including a Safeway in the Fillmore (2025) and the Lucky supermarket on Fulton Street, which is slated to close next month. Hoodline also noted that some Grocery Outlet locations in San Francisco have drawn scrutiny for use of AI-based facial recognition software at entrances, and it remains to be seen whether the Bay Street store will adopt that technology.

topStories.headline: Fisherman's Wharf Forward Construction Wraps Months of Taylor Street Work
topStories.dek: The Port of San Francisco's $10 million revitalization project, which has closed sidewalks and lanes along Taylor Street since December, is nearing the end of its first-phase construction timeline.
topStories.body:
The Port of San Francisco's ambitious Fisherman's Wharf Forward program — a multi-phase, $10 million effort to revitalize the heart of the city's most visited neighborhood — has been reshaping Taylor Street since late 2025 and is reaching the tail end of its initial construction phase this month. The Port's project page notes that temporary sidewalk and traffic lane closures along Taylor Street between Jefferson Street and the Embarcadero were scheduled to continue through August 2026 while demolition and construction work were underway.

The centerpiece of the first phase is a new 5,000-square-foot public plaza on Taylor Street, designed by San Francisco-based firm SITELAB urban studio, replacing the site of the historic Alioto's restaurant. Alioto's, which closed permanently in 2022 after nearly a century in business, was demolished in early 2026 to clear the way for the plaza. The new space will feature wave-shaped seating, picnic tables, benches, string lights, and interpretive signage celebrating the wharf's fishing heritage, with views out to the fishing fleet in the inner lagoon.

Additional near-term improvements include a new overlook along Al Scoma Way and upgraded lighting in the Inner Lagoon to showcase the historic fishing vessels. Longer-term plans under Fisherman's Wharf Forward include seawall reinforcement, flood-proofing of buildings, improvements to facilities for commercial fishers, and new retail leasing on Jefferson Street. The Port has committed to ongoing public engagement to shape those later phases, with a conceptual plan targeted for completion by early 2027.

The project has drawn broad support from city leaders and some concern from commercial fishermen worried about being marginalized on a waterfront that was once the heart of their industry. Fisherman's Wharf attracted more than 10 million visitors in 2024, making it the most-visited destination in San Francisco, according to data cited by the Port.

topStories.headline: Contested Telegraph Hill Tower at 955 Sansome Remains in Planning Limbo
topStories.dek: A proposed 24-story residential tower at the base of Telegraph Hill continues to generate neighborhood opposition years after its original application, with a new SocketSite update flagging activity on the project this month.
topStories.body:
The long-running saga of the proposed residential tower at 955 Sansome Street — at the southeast base of Telegraph Hill — is again in the local spotlight. Real estate tracking site SocketSite posted an update on the project on August 13, noting renewed activity on plans for a supersized building on the parking garage parcel, which have grown dramatically since developer Aralon Properties first filed a preliminary assessment in 2021.

What began as a seven-story, 24-unit proposal has expanded through multiple revisions: to 10 stories, then 16 stories, and ultimately to a 24-story tower that would rise approximately 266 feet above the street — roughly 30 feet taller than the summit of Telegraph Hill itself — under state density bonus provisions that allow developers who include affordable units to exceed local height limits. The most recent plans, filed in early 2024, would yield units including 16 apartments for households earning up to 80% of Area Median Income and 10 for households at up to 120% AMI.

The proposal sits squarely within the city's Northeast Waterfront Historic District, and the influential Telegraph Hill Dwellers, a 700-member neighborhood association that has guarded the neighborhood's views and historic fabric since the mid-1950s, has opposed the project at every iteration. Opponents argue the tower is incompatible with the surrounding historic district and would permanently obstruct bay views from the hill. Aralon, represented by Handel Architects, counters that the project would provide much-needed housing on an underutilized surface parking site.

The project remains under review by the San Francisco Planning Department. No hearing date has been publicly scheduled as of this writing. Residents seeking to follow the case can monitor updates at socketsite.com or through the Telegraph Hill Dwellers at thd.org.

events.title: SF Fleet Week 2026 — Air Show & Navy Ship Tours
events.description: San Francisco Fleet Week runs October 4–12, with the main air show on October 9–11 featuring the Blue Angels, F-22 Raptor Demo, Patriots Jet Team, and Canadian Snowbirds. This year serves as the official West Coast celebration of the U.S. Navy's 250th anniversary, with free Navy ship tours, Fleet Fest at Pier 30/32, and free military band concerts across the waterfront.

events.description: The monthly mass bicycle ride steps off from the Embarcadero at 6:30 PM on the last Friday of the month, passing through North Beach and the northern waterfront. All are welcome; no registration required.

moreNews.headline: Hyde Street Pier Ships Relocated to Mare Island as Reconstruction Continues
moreNews.body: Visitors to San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park will find the historic fleet — including the square-rigger Balclutha — gone from their longtime home at Hyde Street Pier. Since 2025, the museum ships have been moored at Mare Island Naval Shipyard in Vallejo while the pier undergoes a comprehensive rebuild. The NPS has not announced an estimated completion date. The park's Maritime Museum (Aquatic Park Bathhouse) and Visitor Center at 499 Jefferson St. remain open to the public free of charge, and Aquatic Park and Victorian Park are open from sunrise to sunset year-round.

moreNews.headline: Pizza, Bagel & Beer Festival Returns to North Beach — Tickets Reportedly Sold Out
moreNews.body: The fourth annual SF Pizza, Bagel & Beer Festival, hosted by 13-time World Pizza Champion Tony Gemignani in partnership with the San Francisco Italian Athletic Club, took place on August 15 on Stockton and Filbert Streets adjacent to Washington Square Park. The 2026 edition added a live music stage in Washington Square Park featuring swing, jazz, and rockabilly acts throughout the afternoon — a new feature for the event. Vendors included Tony's Pizza Napoletana, Flour + Water Pizzeria, Boichik Bagels, Sierra Nevada, Fieldwork Brewing, and Lagunitas, among dozens of others. Proceeds benefit local nonprofits including the Salesian Boys & Girls Club, Saints Peter & Paul School, and Friends of Washington Square Park. Tickets sold out ahead of the event, consistent with prior years.

moreNews.headline: Caffe Trieste Temporarily Adjusting Hours at Flagship North Beach Location
moreNews.body: The legendary Caffe Trieste at 601 Vallejo St. — North Beach's landmark espresso café open since 1956 and a storied haunt of the Beat Generation — has posted new temporary hours of operation on its website: Sunday through Wednesday, 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM. The café's website notes the reduced schedule but does not specify the reason or duration of the change. Visitors planning an afternoon or evening visit to the flagship location should confirm current hours before going.

restaurants.name: Caffe Trieste
restaurants.description: San Francisco's oldest espresso house, open since 1956, beloved by Beat poets, locals, and visitors for its cappuccinos, pastries, and Saturday afternoon concerts.

restaurants.name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
restaurants.description: Flagship restaurant of 13-time World Pizza Champion Tony Gemignani, serving multiple regional pizza styles from Neapolitan to Detroit in the heart of North Beach.

restaurants.name: Sotto Mare
restaurants.description: Beloved North Beach seafood institution housed in a building dating to 1919, famous for its crab cioppino and fresh daily fish in a classic San Francisco Italian setting.

restaurants.name: Flour + Water Pizzeria
restaurants.description: From the Flour + Water team, this Columbus Avenue spot serves naturally leavened, organic-wheat pizzas with Northern California-sourced toppings, with a casual takeout window on Stockton Street.

restaurants.name: Original Joe's
restaurants.description: A North Beach institution serving classic Italian-American comfort food — prime rib, pastas, and cocktails — in a timeless, lively dining room.

restaurants.name: Vesuvio Cafe
restaurants.description: Iconic two-story Beat Generation saloon established in 1948, just across the alley from City Lights Bookstore, serving affordable drinks amid art and literary memorabilia.

restaurants.name: Comstock Saloon
restaurants.description: Victorian-era saloon in a 1907 building on Columbus Avenue, serving classic cocktails and food alongside free live jazz every night in authentic Barbary Coast surroundings.

restaurants.name: Golden Boy Pizza
restaurants.description: Cash-only North Beach institution serving thick, Sicilian-style pan pizza by the slice since 1978, open late and beloved by night-owls and neighborhood regulars alike.

restaurants.name: Molinari Delicatessen
restaurants.description: North Beach's definitive Italian deli, open since 1896, stacked with house-made salumi, imported cheeses, and legendary sandwiches.

restaurants.name: Caffe Greco
restaurants.description: A North Beach neighborhood staple since 1988, serving espresso drinks, pastries, and light fare in a warm, family-run atmosphere on Columbus Avenue.

restaurants.name: Il Casaro Pizzeria & Mozzarella Bar
restaurants.description: Popular North Beach spot for hand-stretched Neapolitan pies and fresh house-made mozzarella, with a lively, casual atmosphere on Columbus Avenue.

restaurants.name: North Beach Restaurant
restaurants.description: A classic San Francisco Italian restaurant on Stockton Street serving traditional Tuscan cuisine in a warm, family-run setting with a devoted local following.

restaurants.name: Liguria Bakery
restaurants.description: A century-old North Beach institution — open since 1911 — selling only its legendary focaccia, baked fresh each morning until it sells out.

restaurants.name: Reveille Coffee Co.
restaurants.description: A bright, stylish coffee bar at the base of Columbus Avenue serving expertly roasted espresso drinks, avocado toast, and light fare to the North Beach morning crowd.

restaurants.name: Café Zoetrope
restaurants.description: Francis Ford Coppola's North Beach café and wine bar occupying the historic Sentinel Building, serving Italian classics and wines from the Coppola family estate.

restaurants.name: Piccolo Forno
restaurants.description: Intimate North Beach trattoria focused on house-made pastas, Neapolitan-style pizzas, and classic Italian dishes in a snug, neighborhood-welcoming setting on Vallejo Street.

restaurants.name: Surisan
restaurants.description: A locally beloved Fisherman's Wharf spot offering creative Korean-American brunch and dinner with a popular waitlist-only service on weekends.

hotels.name: Argonaut Hotel
hotels.description: AAA Four Diamond boutique hotel housed in the historic Haslett Warehouse at Fisherman's Wharf, featuring bay-view rooms, nautical décor, and Blue Mermaid restaurant; fully refreshed in spring 2025.

hotels.name: Hyatt Centric Fisherman's Wharf San Francisco
hotels.description: 316-room hotel with nautically themed rooms featuring Hyatt Grand Beds and Fisherman's Wharf views, steps from Pier 39 and waterfront dining.

hotels.name: San Francisco Marriott Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: Full-service Marriott at the crossroads of North Beach and Fisherman's Wharf, offering comfortable rooms, meeting space, and walkable access to waterfront attractions.

hotels.name: Hotel Zoe Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: Stylish boutique hotel one block from the waterfront with recently refreshed rooms, valet parking, and a welcoming atmosphere in the heart of Fisherman's Wharf.

hotels.name: Kimpton Alton Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
hotels.description: IHG boutique hotel offering large rooms, a nightly hosted happy hour, and an ideal location steps from Ghirardelli Square and the northern waterfront.

hotels.name: Hotel Zephyr San Francisco
hotels.description: Waterfront hotel with a lively, nautical-industrial aesthetic, outdoor courtyard with games, and direct access to Fisherman's Wharf restaurants and attractions.

hotels.name: Fairmont Heritage Place, Ghirardelli Square
hotels.description: All-suite luxury Fairmont property within the landmark Ghirardelli Square complex, offering full kitchens, private terraces, valet parking, and daily housekeeping.

hotels.name: Wharf Inn
hotels.description: Budget-friendly independent inn steps from the waterfront offering one of the few free parking options at Fisherman's Wharf and easy access to all wharf attractions.

hotels.name: Holiday Inn Express & Suites Fisherman's Wharf by IHG
hotels.description: Convenient IHG property near Ghirardelli Square with complimentary breakfast, clean rooms, and walking distance to the waterfront and cable car lines.

shops.name: City Lights Booksellers & Publishers
shops.description: The nation's first all-paperback bookstore, founded by poet Lawrence Ferlinghetti in 1953 and declared a San Francisco landmark, spanning three floors of new releases, poetry, politics, and literary fiction open daily until midnight.

shops.name: Molinari Delicatessen
shops.description: North Beach's storied Italian deli since 1896, selling house-cured salumi, imported cheeses, olives, and overstuffed sandwiches made to order.

shops.name: Graffeo Coffee Roasting Company
shops.description: Family-run North Beach coffee roaster in operation since 1935, selling its single-blend dark and light roast beans retail and wholesale to Bay Area restaurants.

shops.name: Goorin Bros. Hat Shop
shops.description: The North Beach flagship of San Francisco's own hat company, offering a wide range of fedoras, caps, and specialty headwear in a stylish Columbus Avenue storefront.

shops.name: Biordi Art Imports
shops.description: North Beach institution since 1946 specializing in hand-painted Italian majolica pottery imported directly from artisan studios in Deruta and other Italian regions.

shops.name: XOX Truffles
shops.description: Award-winning North Beach confectionery producing handcrafted truffles in dozens of flavors, with a devoted local following and an inviting shop on Columbus Avenue.

shops.name: Schein & Schein
shops.description: A beloved North Beach shop selling antique maps, prints, and rare cartographic curiosities that has drawn browsers and serious collectors alike for decades.

shops.name: Little City Market
shops.description: A well-stocked neighborhood market and butcher shop on Stockton Street, a go-to for North Beach residents seeking fresh meats, pantry staples, and Italian specialty items.

shops.name: Grocery Outlet
shops.description: The newest grocery anchor at the NorthPoint Shopping Center on Bay Street, offering discounted name-brand groceries, fresh produce, meat, and dairy to the North Beach and Fisherman's Wharf community after opening in August 2026.

artEntertainment.name: Cobb's Comedy Club
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's premier comedy venue since 1982, hosting national touring headliners and local showcases six nights a week in an intimate 400-seat room on Columbus Avenue.

artEntertainment.name: Musée Mécanique
artEntertainment.description: Free-admission, for-profit museum at Pier 45 housing over 300 operational 20th-century penny arcade games and mechanical instruments — one of the world's largest privately owned collections of its kind.

artEntertainment.name: San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park — Maritime Museum & Visitor Center
artEntertainment.type: National park museum and visitor center
artEntertainment.description: The park's Streamline Moderne Maritime Museum and Visitor Center at 499 Jefferson St. are free and open to the public; note that Hyde Street Pier and its historic ships are currently closed for reconstruction.

artEntertainment.name: City Lights Booksellers — Literary Events
artEntertainment.description: Beyond bookselling, the legendary City Lights regularly hosts author readings, political discussions, and literary events in its historic North Beach store, open daily until midnight.

artEntertainment.name: The Beat Museum
artEntertainment.description: Dedicated museum celebrating the Beat Generation writers and artists who made North Beach their home, featuring memorabilia, rare first editions, photographs, and multimedia exhibits.

artEntertainment.name: USS Pampanito
artEntertainment.description: A fully restored World War II fleet submarine open for self-guided tours at Pier 45, operated by the San Francisco Maritime National Park Association.

artEntertainment.name: S.S. Jeremiah O'Brien
artEntertainment.description: One of only two fully operational World War II Liberty Ships in existence, docked at Pier 35 and open for tours and occasional cruises as a living museum of the war's maritime logistics.

artEntertainment.name: Bix
artEntertainment.description: An elegant Gold Street supper club evoking a 1930s speakeasy, with live jazz nightly — solo piano early in the week and a full combo on weekends — alongside a sophisticated cocktail and dinner menu.

artEntertainment.name: Aquarium of the Bay
artEntertainment.description: A nonprofit aquarium at Pier 39 showcasing the marine life of San Francisco Bay through walk-through tunnels, touch pools, and conservation programming.

gymsRecreation.name: Glow Yoga & Wellness
gymsRecreation.type: Yoga and Pilates studio with wellness spa
gymsRecreation.description: North Beach's holistic studio offering Pilates, yoga, barre, and strength classes alongside a wellness spa with red light therapy, massage, and facials in a welcoming community setting.

gymsRecreation.name: Orangetheory Fitness — North Beach
gymsRecreation.description: North Beach outpost of the science-backed, heart-rate-monitored group fitness franchise, offering coached HIIT classes on Columbus Avenue.

gymsRecreation.name: Washington Square Park
gymsRecreation.description: North Beach's beloved community green space bordered by Saints Peter and Paul Church, perfect for tai chi, picnicking, Frisbee, dog walking, and people-watching, with regular free events and festivals.

gymsRecreation.name: Aquatic Park / Victorian Park
gymsRecreation.description: A calm, protected cove at the foot of Hyde Street used year-round by cold-water swimmers, kayakers, and strollers, with the Streamline Moderne bathhouse framing a sweeping bay view; open from sunrise to sunset.

gymsRecreation.name: Fitness SF — Embarcadero
gymsRecreation.description: A well-equipped, full-service fitness center serving the Embarcadero North and Financial District communities with cardio, weight equipment, and group fitness classes.

gymsRecreation.name: Coit Tower / Telegraph Hill Steps
gymsRecreation.type: Landmark park and urban hiking trail
gymsRecreation.description: The iconic Coit Tower atop Telegraph Hill offers panoramic bay views; the Filbert Steps descending to Embarcadero North are one of San Francisco's most popular urban walks, passing through wild garden terraces home to the famous flock of cherry-headed conures.

gymsRecreation.name: Chinatown YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: A community-focused YMCA serving the neighborhoods bordering North Beach and Chinatown, offering gym equipment, fitness classes, and youth programming.

gymsRecreation.name: Pier 39 Embarcadero Waterfront Promenade
gymsRecreation.description: The bayside walkway connecting Pier 39 to the Embarcadero is a popular route for joggers, cyclists, and strollers, offering unobstructed views of the bay, Alcatraz, and the Golden Gate Bridge.
